reasoning: The skill already instructs agents to prefer exact wording and direct evidence, so the nickname-selection error does not warrant duplicating that rule. A more operational answer-form rule can address the recurring name-completion, modifier, category-versus-examples, and grammatical-form mismatches.

edits.target: - Give the concise canonical value at the level of specificity requested. Avoid explanations and redundant qualifiers.
edits.content: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
